observations.text: Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa is publicly presented as a Deluxe Resort hotel combining accommodation, dining, transportation, recreation and proximity to Walt Disney World theme parks.
Public discovery material distinguishes narrower relationships including Club Level benefits, Extended Evening Theme Park Hours and separately reservable Grand Floridian cabanas.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect desktop and mobile discovery and booking paths to determine how clearly lodging, park admission, Club Level benefits, Deluxe Resort privileges and separately purchased products are distinguished before commitment.
dimensions.question: How clearly does Grand Floridian distinguish the base lodging relationship from theme-park admission, tier-specific Resort benefits and separately reservable experiences?
dimensions.reason: The public source set exposes several eligibility and product boundaries, but their prominence and clarity across the complete guest discovery journey have not been systematically tested.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish whether first-time guests consistently understand which benefits arise from lodging, Deluxe Resort status, Club Level status, park admission or separate purchase.
Desktop and mobile ordering, comparative presentation and decision friction have not been systematically inspected.

observations.text: A valid Disney Resort hotel reservation establishes the accommodation relationship and can also create an earlier or broader planning window for certain dining reservations.
Eligible Resort-hotel guests receive an earlier Lightning Lane purchase window, but Lightning Lane remains separately purchased and valid theme-park admission is still required.
Grand Floridian cabanas are separately reservable full-day products restricted to guests of that Resort hotel.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect live room, package, dining, Lightning Lane and cabana reservation flows for payment, cancellation, modification, capacity and entitlement dependencies.
dimensions.question: How does the lodging reservation create base status and planning privileges while park admission, dining, Lightning Lane and cabana commitments remain distinct?
dimensions.reason: The public evidence shows several commitments and eligibility gates layered around the hotel reservation, but their complete contractual and recovery relationships are not established.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish whether lodging, park admission, dining, Lightning Lane and cabana products share inventory, modification or cancellation logic.
The operational consequences of changing or cancelling one component of a multi-product trip remain incomplete.

observations.text: Guests with a valid Disney Resort hotel reservation can make select dining reservations for their length of stay, up to 10 nights, beginning 60 days before arrival.
Eligible Disney Resort hotel guests receive a 7-day advance-purchase window for Lightning Lane passes for eligible stay dates.
Club Level accommodation adds Personalized Guest Services and Disney Signature Services beyond the standard room relationship.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect actual confirmation and pre-arrival communication sequences for how lodging, admission, dining, transportation, Lightning Lane and Club Level privileges are communicated and coordinated.
dimensions.question: What planning privileges and service relationships become available before arrival, and how are they connected to the confirmed lodging relationship?
dimensions.reason: The public evidence identifies meaningful advance-planning privileges, but the actual communication sequence, personalization and cross-product coordination have not been inspected.
unanswered: The current evidence does not establish the actual sequence of pre-arrival messages sent to Grand Floridian guests.
It does not establish whether the Resort proactively reconciles room status, park admission, dining, transportation and experience selections before arrival.

observations.text: Early Theme Park Entry is available to eligible registered Resort-hotel guests on check-in and check-out days, but valid theme-park admission remains separately required.
Grand Floridian provides complimentary monorail, watercraft and bus transportation connecting the Resort with parts of Walt Disney World.
Disney Resort hotels provide accessible paths from arrival areas to the lobby and to accessible guest rooms and other major hotel facilities.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect digital and physical check-in, credential activation, transportation wayfinding, admission verification and accessibility handling at arrival.
dimensions.question: How does arrival activate the lodging relationship while preserving separate admission, credential, transportation and accessibility requirements?
dimensions.reason: The public evidence establishes several arrival-day privileges and requirements, but credential issuance, exception handling and operational handoffs remain incomplete.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish how room status, park admission and eligible Resort benefits are reconciled when credentials fail or trip components are missing.
The physical arrival and accessibility journey has not been directly observed.

observations.text: Club Level rooms and suites create narrower benefits including Royal Palm Club access and Personalized Guest Services.
Early Theme Park Entry requires eligible hotel status plus valid theme-park admission; lodging status alone does not satisfy the park-entry requirement.

Extended Evening Theme Park Hours create a narrower benefit associated with registered guests of Disney Deluxe Resorts and other eligible hotels, and Grand Floridian is explicitly listed as participating.
Grand Floridian cabanas create a separately reserved, Resort-guest-only private-space entitlement inside the broader Resort relationship.
Lightning Lane passes remain separately purchased products even when Resort-hotel status creates an earlier purchase window.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Map the exact entitlement stack for standard-room guests, Club Level guests, park-admission holders, Extended Evening Hours users, Lightning Lane purchasers and cabana renters.
dimensions.question: How do lodging status, accommodation tier, park admission and separately purchased products combine into different guest entitlements during the stay?
dimensions.reason: The case exposes multiple overlapping eligibility layers, but public evidence does not establish whether they represent a unified responsibility architecture or conventional Disney Resort product segmentation.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish whether these entitlements are operationally managed through one guest profile and one recovery structure.
The simpler explanation of conventional resort tiers, admission requirements and ancillary products remains viable.

observations.text: Grand Floridian offers multiple dining formats and select restaurants support advance reservations.
Guests with a valid Disney Resort hotel reservation can make select dining reservations for their entire stay, up to 10 nights, beginning 60 days before arrival.
An in-park dining reservation does not provide theme-park access: valid admission is separately required and a dining reservation does not guarantee access to the park.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect Resort and in-park dining reservation flows, deposits, cancellation terms, admission checks and responsibility when a dining reservation exists but park access fails.
dimensions.question: How do Resort dining reservations, hotel-based advance booking privileges and separate theme-park admission interact without becoming the same entitlement?
dimensions.reason: Disney explicitly separates dining reservation from park-entry entitlement, but the operational handling of conflicts, failures and cross-system recovery is not established.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish who owns recovery when a guest has a valid dining reservation but lacks or loses the required park access.
The degree of integration between hotel, dining and park-admission systems is not established by public evidence.

unanswered: The evidence does not establish the exact expiration time for Club Level access, Resort credentials or other lodging-linked privileges on departure day.
It does not establish whether separately purchased experiences retain independent validity after room checkout.

Club Level lounge access and separately reserved poolside cabanas create more restricted or private zones within the broader shared Resort environment.

observations.text: The core public relationship is a Deluxe Resort hotel stay supported by dining, recreation and complimentary Disney transportation.

Narrower eligibility layers include Club Level services, valid-admission-dependent Early Theme Park Entry, Deluxe-specific Extended Evening Theme Park Hours, separately purchased Lightning Lane passes and Resort-guest-only cabanas.
Disney explicitly demonstrates that one confirmed relationship does not automatically satisfy another: a dining reservation does not guarantee theme-park access.

dimensions.nextEvidence: Test whether these overlapping statuses materially divide customer identity, capacity, responsibility and recovery, or whether they are fully explained by conventional destination-resort segmentation and ancillary products.
dimensions.question: Does Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa demonstrate Role-Partitioned / Multi-Relationship Hospitality Architecture, or is it better explained as a conventional Deluxe destination resort embedded in a larger separately ticketed theme-park ecosystem?
dimensions.reason: The case provides unusually visible layered eligibility boundaries, but conventional destination-resort segmentation remains a strong competing explanation.
unanswered: The evidence does not establish whether lodging, park admission, dining, Club Level, Lightning Lane, cabana and transportation relationships are coordinated through one responsibility architecture.
The simpler explanation of one Deluxe hotel operating inside a larger Disney destination ecosystem with conventional tiers and ancillary products remains viable.
